approach: Write one new design note, docs/design/continuous-landing.md, that makes landing a continuous step of the drain. Once the verifier passes, the job joins the one ordered landing queue (async-drain.md sections 6 and 7). The queue head merges its pull request with the code that exists today (`land_pr` with `merge_via_rest = true`). A job whose checks poll ends pending (`Landing::Waiting`) stays in the queue and is polled again inside the drain; it no longer leaves the drain to wait for a later `athena land --pr`. The self-rebuild becomes a deferred step that no longer holds the `landing` lock against other jobs' landings. I read the code. `LandingQueue` and the `landing` mutex exist. `Drain::land` (drain.rs:1714-1768) holds the lock through `recheck_after_rebase`, `steps.land` and the bookkeeping. `PrLander::land` calls `land_pr` with a poll of 30 attempts × 20 s, so one job can hold the lock for up to 10 minutes (wiring.rs:42-48). `rebuild_if_due` (drain.rs:2402-2424) takes the same lock, and `finish` calls it only after `ItemEnd::Landed` (drain.rs:2428-2431). So a job's own rebuild already falls after its own landing record. The rebuild reaches only other jobs' spans, through lock contention. The note says this plainly. It does not call the rebuild a measurement effect for the job's own span. It asks the next review to report rebuild time separately, so the lock contention it causes stays visible. The note states the review's figures with sources: 440.1 of 464.5 min in landing and rebuild, about 21 min elsewhere, idle 16070.4/366. It labels 420.0 min as the review's prediction and names the measurement: the median over the newest 20 landings (`THROUGHPUT_WINDOW`) from the verifier's end to the landing record, against 464.5 (stage 440.1). It covers alternatives, risks, out of scope, ordered build jobs and the duty to cite review 20261105-070420-vq95. Small additive edits go in async-drain.md (pointers), docs/decisions.md (D155) and CHANGELOG.md (one Unreleased entry). No code or governance file changes.

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing REST merge in `land_pr` (the `merge_via_rest` path), run by the queue head, as the 'automatic merge'. Do not depend on a host auto-merge setting.
decisions.reason: The merge call, the wait for checks, the landing intent and landing records and the merged-content check exist and are tested (crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs:228-300; native-pr-landing.md section 5). Host squash-only and linear-history rules (docs/system-facts.md) are already handled there. The new work is when the merge starts and who waits for it, not how it merges.

rejected.option: Enable the host's native auto-merge on the pull request at enqueue
rejected.why: It needs a repository setting the code does not show to be on (an open Host question). The merge would also happen outside the ordered queue, so order and the landing-intent write (records-history.md) would no longer hold.

rejected.option: Add a new merge code path for the drain
rejected.why: It duplicates `land_pr` and its safety checks for no saving.

decisions.choice: Release the worker at verifier pass. The queue head does the rebase, CI wait and merge. A job whose poll ends pending (`Landing::Waiting`) stays in the ordered queue and is polled again inside the drain (the parked CI wait of async-drain.md sections 6 and 7). It is not passed over for a later `athena land --pr`.
decisions.reason: Today `Drain::land` holds the `landing` lock for the whole poll, up to 30 × 20 s (drain.rs:1715; wiring.rs:42-48). A pending poll gives `Landing::Waiting` (drain.rs:3136-3156), the job is marked 'waiting to merge' with its PR open (drain.rs:1761-1765), `work` returns `ItemEnd::Waiting` (drain.rs:1860) and the item is passed over (drain.rs:2511). A later, separate `athena land --pr` finishes it (drain.rs:128-130). That later step is the most likely home of a 440-minute median, since the median CI run is 583 s (warm-baseline-build.md 2.1). The measured span runs from verifier end to the later of the landing outcome and the landing record (status.rs:648-650, 805-813), so waiting in a serial tail is the cause, not work.

rejected.why: async-drain.md section 9 alternative a: jobs would land racing, with no order and no conflict return.
It does not address the queue, the passed-over Waiting jobs or the rebuild share of a stage that is more than 20 times the median CI run.

decisions.choice: Defer the self-rebuild to a safe point where no job is in a landing or records stage, so it no longer takes the `landing` lock ahead of other jobs' landings. A failed rebuild still holds landing and starts no new producers. Ask the next review to report rebuild time separately, because the rebuild adds to later jobs' spans through the lock.
decisions.reason: `finish` calls `rebuild_if_due()` only after `ItemEnd::Landed` (drain.rs:2428-2431), so a job's own rebuild falls after its own landing record and is outside its own span (status.rs:805-813). `rebuild_if_due` takes the same `landing` mutex as every landing (drain.rs:2403 and 1715). So it adds to the spans of later jobs that wait on that lock. hestia.md:277 says no record separates the rebuild, so the code cannot show how much of the 440.1 min it is. Reporting it separately lets the next review see the contention and stops it overstating the saving.

rejected.option: Say part of the 420.0 min is a measurement change because the rebuild leaves the span
rejected.why: The code shows a job's own rebuild already falls after its landing record, so this claim is wrong.

rejected.option: Count the whole saving as latency removed
rejected.why: hestia.md:277 says no record separates the rebuild. Claiming all of it would be unmeasured.

decisions.choice: Make the first build job a measurement of the 440.1 min by phase: wait for the drain, queue wait, lock wait, CI poll, time in Waiting before a later `athena land --pr`, merge and rebuild. It uses the existing timestamps. Raise limits only afterwards.
decisions.reason: The snapshot has no records or THROUGHPUT.md, and the code cannot say which phase dominates. The 420.0 min is the review's prediction. The note labels it that and builds the evidence step first.

rejected.why: A design that cannot show where 440.1 min goes risks fixing the wrong wait.

D155 and the note refer to D140 and to async-drain.md without the words 'amends', 'supersedes' or 'superseded by' next to a decision id. Add one CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

risks.risk: Ordering: releasing the worker at verifier pass lets later jobs enqueue while an earlier one waits on CI, and they could land out of order.
risks.mitigation: The note keeps one landing at a time under the existing ordered queue (async-drain.md section 6) and keeps first-in first-out by verifier pass. A job in Waiting keeps its place at the head and is polled again. The merged-content check in `land_pr` stays as the safety net.

risks.risk: Rebuild failure: deferring the rebuild could let jobs land on a main that Athena cannot build.
risks.mitigation: The note keeps the section 7 rule (D140): the rebuild runs when no job is in a landing or records stage, and a failed rebuild holds landing and starts no new producers. The rebuild result is reported separately from the landing record.

risks.risk: Merge conflicts: a job waiting in the queue meets a moved main.
risks.mitigation: The note reuses the section 6 rebase, the held-back conflict case, `max_conflict_returns` and the re-check rule (`rebase_needs_recheck`; `recheck_after_rebase` at drain.rs:1716). It says the real conflict hold wiring is a dependency of the build jobs.

risks.risk: The saving is misread. A job's own rebuild already falls after its landing record (drain.rs:2428-2431), so it is not in that job's span, and the rebuild shows up only as lock contention in later jobs' spans. A review that does not separate the rebuild cannot tell how much of the saving is contention removed.
risks.mitigation: The note labels 420.0 min as the review's prediction and derives the implied remainder (464.5 - 420.0 = 44.5 min). It explains the rebuild as lock contention, asks the next review to report rebuild time separately, and compares the 20 newest landings after the change.

risks.risk: The 440.1 minutes may be mostly the wait before the drain reaches the job, or time in Waiting before a later `athena land --pr`, so the design would remove less than predicted.
risks.mitigation: The note makes the phase split (including Waiting as its own phase) the first build job and states that the saving depends on it.

risks.risk: The boundary or personal-data scan, or the backtest link scan, fails on new prose.
risks.mitigation: Verify the new and edited files hold no banned word, no email-like text and no 'amends', 'supersedes' or 'superseded by' next to a decision id; `cargo test --locked` would catch each.
